items.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Daniel Jones could wait to sign with a new team if he goes unclaimed on waivers.
items.text: The belief is that Jones won’t be claimed on waivers, since any team that claims him would inherit his remaining contract with the Colts. Instead, Jones will likely pass through waivers and become a free agent, but he could delay signing with a new team immediately and instead opt to wait and see what other options may become available during the season. items.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports 49ers RT Colton McKivitz will likely miss the remainder of the season after suffering fracturing and dislocating his ankle in Week 11’s win over the Vikings.
items.text: If you saw this injury during the game, you immediately knew this would likely be a season-ender. McKivitz’s left leg twisted unnaturally after a play in the second quarter, and the 30-year-old tackle was carted off the field shortly after. While we hope for the best, we fully expect the team to announce McKivitz’s season is over at some point this week. McKivitz was replaced by Vederian Lowe, who will presumably be the Niners’ starting right tackle moving forward. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports DK Metcalf’s actions will be “reviewed for potential additional discipline, including suspension” following his ejection in Week 11 against the Eagles.
items.text: Metcalf was ejected from Sunday’s game against the Eagles after receiving his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. The 28-year-old receiver ended the day with one catch for two yards and had two altercations with Eagles CB Cooper DeJean before he was sent to the locker room. Metcalf will almost certainly receive a fine from the league in the coming days, but a suspension could put him in line to miss Week 12’s game against the Broncos. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Deebo Samuel caught 3-of-4 targets for 20 yards in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings, adding 27 yards on two carries.
items.text: Samuel continued to operate as the primary gadget player for a 49ers team now with Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, and George Kittle all fully healthy. While that role carries per-touch upside given the space he should have when receiving the ball, fantasy managers are likely forced to view Samuel more as a potential Flex than a viable weekly starter. That will remain true ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the Seahawks. - Mark Garcia

items.title: George Kittle caught all three passes for 34 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
items.text: Kittle got to work early, capping off the opening drive with a touchdown from 17 yards out before adding a second touchdown early in the second quarter. The team would score again on their subsequent possession before the defense tacked on a pick-six on the following play, capping passing volume and leading to the low target total for the veteran tight end in the process. Even so, Kittle continued to showcase his elite athleticism, body control, and strength on his two scores and remains a surefire TE1 heading into another difficult matchup against the Seahawks in Week 12. - Mark Garcia

items.title: Keenan Allen caught 3-of-4 targets for 38 yards in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
items.text: Allen was hardly used in the first half as George Kittle and Mike Evans did all the heavy lifting but came alive in the third quarter to get his name in the box score. The 49ers’ most recent addition provides yet another offensive weapon alongside Evans, Kittle, Christian McCaffrey, and Deebo Samuel, all of whom are now healthy as the team continues its press toward the only bye out of the NFC. Allen will be a difficult start in fantasy with the other supporting cast fully healthy as they prepare to face the Seahawks in Week 12. - Mark Garcia

items.title: Mike Evans caught 6-of-7 targets for 109 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings.
items.text: Fantasy managers took a collective sigh of relief after Evans was shown on the sideline grimacing in the first quarter. The team would never pass an injury update for their veteran star, who would later connect with quarterback Brock Purdy in the second quarter from four yards out to push the team’s lead to 21-10. The defense would step up with a pick-six on Minnesota’s subsequent possession, allowing the 49ers to coast to the win in the second half. items.title: Christian McCaffrey rushed 12 times for 49 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 11 win over the Vikings, adding 13 yards on two receptions.
items.text: McCaffrey found the end zone for the 14th time this season, marking his ninth consecutive game with a touchdown after failing to find paint in Week 1 against the Rams in Australia. The modest carry total and receiving total were more a comment on how much of a stranglehold the 49ers had on the game than anything else, coasting in the second half after jumping out to a 28-10 lead in the second quarter. The starters would then rest for the team’s final two possessions following McCaffrey’s fourth quarter touchdown. McCaffrey remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 12 meeting with the division rival

items.title: Brock Purdy completed 21-of-26 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns in the 49ers’ 35-10, Week 11 win over the Vikings.
items.text: Purdy and the 49ers controlled the tempo throughout against the aggressive Minnesota defense, expertly handling the blitz as the 49ers jumped out to a 21-10 lead in the second quarter by finding paint on three of their first four possessions. The lead was extended on a pick-six shortly thereafter, allowing the 49ers to coast to their ninth victory of the season. The team now has a stranglehold on the once-competitive NFC West and the inside track to the only bye out of the conference, with only the four teams in the NFC North threatening that claim. items.title: Jauan Jennings caught 3-of-6 targets for 20 yards in the Vikings’ Week 11 loss to the 49ers.
items.text: Jennings operated in a familiar WR3 role for the Vikings despite the absence of Jordan Addison, with Tai Felton getting the start on the perimeter opposite Justin Jefferson. Fantasy managers that thought they were pulling a fast one by adding Jennings are likely better off scooping Felton as a viable Flex for as long as Addison remains sidelined. - Mark Garcia
